en: Typhoon Haiyan in 2013 had sustained winds of 315 km/h, making it one of the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded.
Mount Mayon in Albay is a highly active stratovolcano famous for its perfect conical shape and frequent explosive eruptions.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
The Zambales ophiolite complex contains large deposits of chromite, which is the primary ore used to extract the metal chromium.
The fertile volcanic ash soil, known as andisol, surrounding Mount Pinatubo provides essential nutrients for local farmers to grow abundant crops today.
Olympus Mons on Mars is a massive shield volcano that stands about 22 kilometers high, making it the tallest mountain in the solar system.
Filipino farmers traditionally use the star cluster Balatik, also known as Orion's Belt, to signal the beginning of the dry planting season.
The Tycho crater on the Moon is a prominent impact crater named after the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe and features distinct bright rays.
The city of Baguio experiences a subtropical highland climate, resulting in average annual temperatures of 18 degrees Celsius, much cooler than Metro Manila.
Jupiter's moon Europa has a smooth, icy surface that scientists believe hides a massive liquid water ocean beneath its frozen crust.
Pumice is a highly vesicular rock formed during the explosive 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo when frothy lava cooled rapidly.
The anemometer, invented by Leon Battista Alberti in 1450, is the specific meteorological instrument used to measure the speed of the wind.
